newsitem.title: USA: US junk bond new deals may see another $3 bln week.
newsitem.headline: US junk bond new deals may see another $3 bln week.

text.p: After selling well over $3 billion in new junk bonds over the past week, issuers and underwriters are expected to mount a repeat performance starting next Monday, syndicate officials said.
Dealers are currently set to price 16 new junk bond issues totalling around $2.8 billion in new junk bonds in the week ahead, market sources said.
But many of the deals could be increased in size to meet tremendous investor demand, bringing the total to over $3 billion once again, they noted.
Any fears that the hot new-issue market was not sustainable evaporated on Friday, when AMG Data Services reported strong net new cash inflows for the latest week.
Cash inflows to junk bond mutual funds surged to a healthy $374 million after experiencing slight net outflows of $31.6 million in the prior reporting period, AMG reported.
Market sources noted next week's calendar will consist of diverse group of deals including the first junk bond offering from a pure-play internet service provider.
Verio Inc plans to sell $150 million in seven-year senior notes in a private placement via Merrill Lynch & Co.
The Denver-based company is building a national internet access network targeting business customers, sources said.
The notes will be prefunded for 2.5 years.

Another deal that is likely to draw market interest is a $125 million private placement of seven-year senior discount notes from Chase Telecommunications Inc via Credit Suisse First Boston, sources said.

Chase's transaction represents the first zero coupon offering from a start-up telecommunications company in many months. The deal is likely to include contingent warrants to attract investor interest, sources said.

Market sources said if the offering is successful, other telecommunications and media issuers, such as TeleWest Communications Plc, may be more likely to sell zero coupon paper in the market in the coming weeks.
TeleWest, a U.K. cable company, is expected to raise $300 million in a junk nbond offering in late June or July via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette, sources said.

Other deals for next week include a $255 million offering from a holding company of TV Azteca, Mexico's second largest broadcaster, and a $300 million junk bond refinancing from Specialty Retailers Inc, a unit of Stage Stores Inc, via CSFB.
In the investment-grade sector, next week is shaping up to be active for new issues, syndicate sources said.
Bayerische Landesbank is expected to sell $1 billion in 10-year debt in a global offering via Merrill Lynch.
Rheinische Hypothekenbank may sell $750 million in 10-year global debt in a 144a private placement, sources said.
Hartford Life may also sell $600 million in debt in a multi-tranche offering via Goldman Sachs & Co, they said.
